content.title: About
content.content: Cheese is a dairy food made from the curds of milk, most often from cows, goats, sheep, or buffalo. Milk is curdled, drained, and often pressed, salted, and aged, producing thousands of varieties that range from fresh and soft to hard and aged. Cheese is eaten on its own, with bread and fruit, and used in cooking in countless dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese has been made for thousands of years as a way to preserve milk.
Thousands of varieties exist, differing in milk type, bacteria and molds used, and aging time.
Cheeses range from fresh (cottage cheese, mozzarella) to soft, semi-hard, hard (parmesan), and blue.
Aged cheeses are generally lower in lactose than fresh cheeses.
Some cheeses are made with animal rennet and others with microbial or plant-based coagulants.

items.title: Rich in protein and calcium
items.content: Cheese provides protein and calcium, which support muscles, bones, and teeth.

items.title: Provides vitamin B12 and phosphorus
items.content: These nutrients support red blood cell formation and bone health.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function.

items.title: Often lower in lactose
items.content: Aged hard cheeses contain very little lactose and are often tolerated by people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Flavorful and filling
items.content: A small amount of cheese adds a lot of flavor and helps you feel full.

items.title: Sodium and saturated fat
items.content: Many cheeses are high in sodium and saturated fat, so portion size matters, especially for people limiting salt or saturated fat.

items.title: Milk allergy and lactose
items.content: Cheese contains milk protein, so people with milk allergy should avoid it, and fresh cheeses contain some lactose.

items.title: Listeria
items.content: Soft and unpasteurized cheeses can carry Listeria bacteria. Pregnant women, older adults, and people with weakened immunity should avoid them or follow healthcare advice.

items.title: Tyramine and medications
items.content: Aged cheeses are high in tyramine, which can be a problem for people taking MAOI antidepressants. Ask a healthcare professional if you take them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese can be eaten on its own, on bread and crackers, with fruit and nuts, grated onto pasta, soups, and salads, melted in sandwiches and pizzas, or baked into dishes. Choose smaller portions of strongly flavored cheeses. Let cheese warm slightly before serving for better flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cheese in the refrigerator wrapped in wax paper, parchment, or cheese paper, then loosely in plastic, so it can breathe. Hard cheeses keep for several weeks, while soft and fresh cheeses should be eaten by the date on the package. If hard cheese develops mold, cut off at least about 2.5 cm (1 inch) around it, but discard soft cheese with mold. Freezing can change the texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Green Enchilada Sauce (item 4502) is a fragrant Mexican sauce made from tomatoes, green chilies, cilantro and lime. It delivers a bright, mildly spicy flavor with fresh herb notes and can be used as a base for casseroles or as a dip.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A traditional Mexican sauce commonly served with corn tortilla dishes.
The green color comes from fresh green chilies and cilantro, without artificial coloring.
Regional variations exist: Yucatán versions add avocado, while Oaxacan recipes use extra lime juice.
Often used in vegetarian meals as a flavorful alternative to meat fillings.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Lime and green chilies provide a high amount of vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Cilantro and tomatoes are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The sauce is low‑calorie, making it a good choice for diet‑friendly meals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cilantro and chilies stimulate bile production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: The chilies can cause discomfort for those with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Cilantro allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cilantro.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lime makes the sauce acidic; people with gastritis should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Pour the sauce over baked enchiladas, use it as a chicken marinade, add it to tacos, or serve it as a dip for nachos and vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size containers for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: The chocolate ice cream bar (item 440) is a frozen dessert made from creamy ice cream coated with a thin layer of milk chocolate. It combines a smooth ice‑cream texture with a crunchy chocolate shell, making it a popular treat year‑round.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate ice‑cream bar was introduced in the United States in the 1920s.
The chocolate coating protects the ice cream from melting, allowing the bar to stay solid at slightly higher temperatures.
Emulsifiers and stabilizers are often added to keep the cream smooth after freezing.
Variants around the world may include nuts, caramel, or fruit pieces.
Bars are usually sold in individual wrappers, which makes them easy to transport and vending‑machine friendly.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Dairy ice cream provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk ingredients supply vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates and fats offers a fast source of energy.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can lift mood.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Ice cream contains a notable amount of water, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Bars often contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy components may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Nut and soy allergies
items.content: Some recipes use nuts or soy lecithin, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Melting if stored improperly
items.content: Storing above –12 °C can cause the chocolate shell to crack and the ice cream to melt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bar slowly, allowing the chocolate coating to soften slightly while the ice cream releases its flavor. It’s convenient for on‑the‑go snacking, post‑workout treats, or as a dessert after a meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once removed from the wrapper, consume within 30 minutes to prevent melting. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Pregestimil is a ready‑to‑feed infant formula designed for newborns with increased nutritional needs, including preterm infants, low‑birth‑weight babies, and those with digestive sensitivities. It contains easily digestible proteins, DHA, ARA, and prebiotics to support gut microbiota.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is specifically engineered for infants who have limited tolerance to standard formulas.
It includes a lactulose‑derived prebiotic that promotes the growth of beneficial bacteria.
Enfamil Pregestimil has undergone clinical trials demonstrating its effectiveness in weight gain for preterm infants.
Available in 380 ml ready‑to‑feed bottles, convenient for daily hospital use.
Enriched with B‑vitamins, iron, and zinc to support overall development.

items.title: Supports growth and weight gain
items.content: A balanced ratio of protein, fat, and carbohydrates provides the energy and building blocks needed for rapid growth in preterm infants.

items.title: Contains DHA and ARA
items.content: Omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids aid brain and visual system development.

items.title: Easily digestible proteins
items.content: Hydrolyzed proteins reduce the workload on an immature gastrointestinal tract.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Prebiotics stimulate beneficial bacteria, lowering the risk of dysbiosis.

items.title: Enriched with micronutrients
items.content: Vitamins and minerals (vitamin D, iron, zinc) contribute to overall physiological development.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Infants with confirmed cow’s milk or whey protein allergy should use hypoallergenic formulas.

items.title: Heat exposure
items.content: Store the formula in a cool place; temperatures above 25 °C shorten shelf life.

items.title: Expiration control
items.content: After opening, use within 48 hours and keep refrigerated.

items.title: Does not replace breastfeeding
items.content: The product is intended to supplement or replace breast milk only under medical guidance.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the ready‑to‑feed formula in a sterile nipple at body temperature (about 37 °C). Before use, gently shake the bottle, check for any sediment or off‑odor. If warming is needed, place the bottle in warm water; do not use a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened bottles in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate and use within 48 hours. Discard if the product changes color, odor, or taste.

content.title: About
content.content: Paella is a traditional Spanish dish originating from Valencia. Its base is short‑grain rice (such as Arborio or Bomba) cooked in a wide, shallow pan (paellera) with broth, olive oil, saffron, and a variety of add‑ins: seafood, chicken, rabbit, vegetables, and chorizo sausage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional paella is cooked over an open fire using charcoal for a distinctive smoky flavor.
Saffron, which gives the dish its golden hue, is one of the most expensive spices in the world.
There are several regional versions: seafood paella, Valencian paella (chicken and rabbit), and mixed paella (meat and seafood).
The rice is not stirred during cooking, allowing a crispy crust called “socarrat” to form on the bottom.
Paella has become a symbol of Spanish cuisine and is often served at festivals and family celebrations.

items.title: Rich source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides sustained energy and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Complete protein from meat and seafood
items.content: Chicken, rabbit, seafood, and chorizo supply all essential amino acids.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil adds monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Saffron, vegetables, and seafood contribute vitamin C, B‑vitamins, iron, and magnesium.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Saffron and olive oil are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: People allergic to shellfish or fish may react to seafood paella.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Broths and cured meats can increase the dish’s salt level.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Generous amounts of oil and sausage raise the calorie count.

items.title: Heavy‑metal exposure
items.content: Some seafood may contain trace amounts of cadmium or mercury; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve paella hot straight from the pan. Eat with a fork or spoon, optionally squeezing fresh lemon juice over it. Garnish with chopped parsley or basil and a light side salad if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of broth or water to restore moisture. Paella can be frozen for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Wine Spritzer is a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage made by mixing wine juice with carbonated water and sometimes a hint of fruit flavorings. It offers a light fruity taste, moderate sweetness, and pleasant fizz, making it a popular alternative to traditional alcoholic cocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wine Spritzer originated in Europe in the early 20th century as a lighter alternative to full‑strength wines.
There are many flavor variations: lemon, berry, orange, and even herbal blends.
The drink is often served in tall glasses with ice and a citrus wedge for extra aroma.
Because its alcohol content is usually below 0.5 %, it is considered suitable for driving.
In some countries, wine spritzers are classified as non‑alcoholic if the alcohol level is under 0.5 %.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: The combination of wine juice and sparkling water contains far fewer calories than typical sweet drinks.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Wine juice is rich in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Improved hydration
items.content: Carbonated water promotes better hydration compared with plain juice.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Gentle fizz can aid faster digestion.

items.title: Reduces overeating risk
items.content: Refreshing taste and moderate sweetness help quench thirst without triggering strong hunger.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Although low, the alcohol level may be a concern for those who completely avoid alcohol; always check the label.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some versions contain added sugars, increasing the calorie count.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs may experience discomfort from fizzy drinks.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Fruit flavorings can contain traces of allergens such as citrus.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the spritzer chilled in a glass with ice and a slice of lemon or lime. It pairs well with light snacks, salads, or seafood. For variety, add fresh berries or mint.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 2–3 days and reseal tightly.
